assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Six tenths of the land in agriculture along the Niles: the breadbasket the nation can be again.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: The Nile dams gave six tenths of the power before the war.

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: What lies under the land already earns; the task is to turn the rent into lasting assets.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Territory to farm, mine, power and protect.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 40.2% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Kenana Sugar Company
items.text: The only sugar factory that kept working through the war: about 200,000 tonnes in 2023–24 and 125,000 in 2024–25.

items.name: Al Teital Advance Industries
items.text: A Khartoum sesame-oil maker that employed 300 people before the war and is bringing its factory back.

items.name: Practical Action
items.text: Repaired sixteen solar water yards and built ten more in Kassala and Gedarif: safe water for more than 20,000 families.

items.name: Bankak
items.text: The Bank of Khartoum’s mobile banking app: salaries, money from relatives abroad and aid payments, when cash ran out.
